title: Restore a trusted relative newc archive separately
goal: Create, inspect and restore a small newc cpio archive of known regular files without replacing originals.
challenge: Archive the two supplied regular files with literal NUL names. Verify exact members and retained hash, restore to a new empty destination, then compare contents and modes. Explain why this does not admit arbitrary archives safely.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/textarchive-cpio.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/textarchive-cpio.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command:
here && fresh source members.bin expected.txt original.sha copy.cpio archive.sha listed.txt restore && mkdir source && printf 'note
' > source/note.txt && printf 'spaced
' > source/'space name.txt' && chmod 0600 source/note.txt source/'space name.txt' && printf '%s\0' note.txt 'space name.txt' > members.bin && printf '%s
' note.txt 'space name.txt' > expected.txt && sha256sum source/note.txt source/'space name.txt' > original.sha
steps.explanation: Only these two relative regular files are trusted inputs; no links, devices, absolute paths or parent members. This is practice, not a hostile-archive importer.

steps.command: here && dir_ok source && test -f source/note.txt && test ! -L source/note.txt && test -f source/'space name.txt' && test ! -L source/'space name.txt' && ( cd "$w/source" && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w/source" && timeout -k 1s 8s cpio -0 -o -H newc --quiet < ../members.bin > ../copy.cpio ) && test "$(stat -c %s copy.cpio)" -le 65536 && sha256sum copy.cpio > archive.sha
steps.explanation: newc is explicitly selected. NUL input preserves the space name. The timeout and measured size bound this trusted fixture, not arbitrary input.
steps.expected: A private bounded archive; original hashes retained separately.

steps.command: here && dir_ok source && sha256sum -c archive.sha && timeout -k 1s 8s cpio -it --quiet < copy.cpio > listed.txt && cmp expected.txt listed.txt && fresh restore && mkdir restore && dir_ok restore && ( cd "$w/restore" && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w/restore" && timeout -k 1s 8s cpio -id --no-absolute-filenames --quiet < ../copy.cpio ) && cmp source/note.txt restore/note.txt && cmp source/'space name.txt' restore/'space name.txt' && test "$(stat -c %a restore/note.txt)" = 600 && test "$(stat -c %a restore/'space name.txt')" = 600 && sha256sum -c original.sha
steps.explanation: Inspect before extraction, and use a fresh empty separate target. --no-absolute-filenames alone is not a general archive safety guarantee. Hashes detect change against a trusted retained reference; they do not establish authenticity.
steps.expected: Exact members, contents and mode; original source unchanged.

hints: A listing is not a contents comparison.
Use exact known relative names and a fresh destination.
